X.why: The runway-crossing hook is genuinely striking and the 'both sides' records framing is promising. But the narration is mostly scene-setting. 'Since July 2026, no routine checks' is a bare claim with no explanation of why. 'Historians on both sides count fourteen' sounds tidy and the title is repeated back to me without nuance. It is competent but does not yet tell me anything I didn't know.
X.moment_you_would_leave_or_doubt: 'This is why everyone fought over it' – the video has said nothing yet about why, so it reads as filler. I'd also doubt the flat '14 sieges' count, since the number depends on how you define a siege. I'd give it a few more minutes, watching for any hedging on that.

Y.why: It opens with a quote war and leans on 'key of the Mediterranean', which is the most worn cliché in Gibraltar writing. The quotes are sourced, but the border hook, the best thing here, is reduced to wallpaper behind a quotation. 'A Spanish historian' and 'a British one' flatten both sides into one cliché each. The key metaphor is repeated again at the end ('this key'), which feels like a thesis and is oversimplifying.
Y.moment_you_would_leave_or_doubt: 'This is why everyone fought over this key' – the whole premise collapses into one metaphor. Combined with the unqualified '14 sieges' claim, it sounds like clickbait with footnotes. I'd also be suspicious that the 'two years later' pairing of 1860 and 1862 is presented as a dialogue between historians, when it's likely coincidence.

Z.why: It is the only version that adds substance and complicates its own headline: 'Only five changed who ruled it' tells me the video knows a siege and a change of rule are different things, which is the distinction the title blurs. It also explains the border change ('new UK–EU treaty'), which makes the opening feel informed instead of decorative. 'But look where it sits' lets the map do the work without a cliché. Sources are modest and honest.
Z.moment_you_would_leave_or_doubt: 'Only five changed who ruled it' – I'd check this immediately. If it means the Moorish captures of 1309 and 1333, the 1462 Spanish capture, 1704 and the 1469 Spanish-held episode, I'd want the video to name them. Also, 'Since July' without a year and the single source line are slight weaknesses. If the five aren't clearly listed or are wrong, I'd leave.

one_change_to_the_best_version: Name the five changes of ruler on screen, with dates, while the line 'Only five changed who ruled it' plays, so the claim is verifiable on the spot. Also add the year to 'Since July' and restore the García Sanz source.
